elements.element: Customer owns all deliverables created for it.
elements.evidence: Section 5.5 provides that the Company owns “all right, title and interest” in “all deliverables ... created for the Company under this Agreement.”

elements.element: Customer owns all work product created for it.
elements.evidence: Section 5.5 expressly gives the Company ownership of all work product created for it under the Agreement.

elements.element: Vendor assigns to Customer all of Vendor’s right, title and interest in the deliverables.
elements.evidence: HDI “hereby assigns to the Company all right, title and interest it may have in such deliverables.”

elements.element: Vendor assigns to Customer all of Vendor’s right, title and interest in the work product.
elements.evidence: The same present assignment expressly covers the work product.

elements.element: Vendor retains ownership of its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: The clause states that “HDI shall retain ownership of its pre-existing intellectual property.”

elements.element: Vendor grants Customer a licence to Vendor intellectual property embedded in the deliverables.
elements.evidence: HDI grants the Company a licence to “any HDI intellectual property embedded in the deliverables.”

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The embedded-IP licence is expressly described as “perpetual.”

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The embedded-IP licence is expressly described as “irrevocable.”

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The embedded-IP licence is expressly described as “royalty-free.”

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The clause defines Company Data to include customer, order, transaction and user data and expressly states that the Company “retains all rights in the Company Data.”

elements.element: No joint ownership arises in the deliverables, work product or Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly provides that nothing in the Agreement creates joint ownership of the deliverables, work product or Company Data.

elements.element: Vendor owns generic tools.
elements.evidence: The clause reserves only HDI’s pre-existing intellectual property. It does not reserve generic tools generally, including generic tools developed during performance.

elements.element: Vendor owns know-how.
elements.evidence: There is no express reservation of HDI’s know-how, and the broad assignment of all work product created for the Company could encompass project-developed know-how.

elements.element: Customer receives a licence to the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The operative licence covers only HDI intellectual property embedded in the deliverables, not the deliverables themselves. The Company instead owns the deliverables.

elements.element: The licence to the deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Although no licence to the deliverables is granted, the Company receives unrestricted ownership through a present assignment, which is not temporally limited and substantively provides at least perpetual rights.

elements.element: The licence to the deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The Company’s ownership is effected by an unconditional present assignment with no revocation or reversion mechanism, substantively providing irrevocable rights.

elements.element: The licence to the deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: The clause does not expressly state that any licence is worldwide; the only express licence is for embedded HDI intellectual property and omits territorial scope.

elements.element: The licence to the deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The Company owns the deliverables without an ongoing royalty condition, and the separate licence for embedded HDI intellectual property is expressly royalty-free.

elements.element: The licence permits Customer to use the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The Company’s ownership of all right, title and interest in the deliverables substantively includes the right to use them.

elements.element: The licence permits Customer to modify the deliverables.
elements.evidence: Ownership of all right, title and interest in the deliverables substantively gives the Company the right to modify them, subject to the embedded Vendor-IP licence.

elements.element: The licence permits Customer to sublicense the deliverables.
elements.evidence: As owner of all right, title and interest in the deliverables, the Company can authorize third parties to use them, although the embedded Vendor-IP licence itself does not expressly include sublicensing.

elements.element: Customer may exercise its rights in the deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: The Company’s ownership rights are not restricted by field of use and therefore encompass use for its business.

result.reason: The redline fully implements the preferred position through Company ownership, a present assignment, HDI’s pre-existing-IP reservation, the required embedded-IP licence, Company Data ownership and an express prohibition on joint ownership. The fallback is not fully satisfied because generic tools and know-how are not reserved generally, no licence to the deliverables as such is granted, and worldwide scope is omitted. The change is not minimal because it additionally assigns ownership of the Site and all Content, beyond the specified deliverables, work product and Customer Data requirements. No contradiction with the retained liaison provision is apparent.
